learning_outcomes.text: To have the capacity to design, develop, implement, manage, and improve products, systems, and processes in various industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational, or experimental techniques.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.
To apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
To possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
To know and apply the knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry.

syllabus_topics: Types of crystals by geometric shape. Crystalline systems
Relationship between interplanar distance and surface density
Slip planes and directions. Slip systems
Cohesive forces. Elastic modulus. Study of energies
Thermal and mechanical resistance of a pure metal
Observation levels of a metal. General properties of metals
Conditions for the formation of solid solutions by substitution
Conditions for the formation of solid solutions by insertion
Interstitial sites in body-centered cubic (bcc), face-centered cubic (fcc), and hexagonal close-packed (hcp) systems
Reactions in diagrams. Eutectic. Eutectoid. Peritectic. Peritectoid. Monotectic. Monotectoid.
Rules for interpreting diagrams. Portevin rules
Properties of constituents present in steels and cast irons
Metals. Light metals and non-light metals
Magnesium, Beryllium, Nickel, and Titanium: properties and applications of these metals
Bronzes and brasses: classification and properties
Lead, Tin, and Zinc: properties and applications
General introduction to these types of materials
Crystalline structures of simple ceramic materials: AX, AmXp, AmBnXp type structures. Ceramics formed by silicates. Imperfections in crystalline structures.

Phase diagrams of ceramic materials: Functional engineering ceramics. Properties of industrial ceramics: mechanical, thermal, electrical, and electronic properties. Magnetic properties. Introduction to processing.
Glasses, properties of glasses, and glass forming. Glass-ceramics
Energy band model and electrical conductivity
Intrinsic semiconductors. Electrical conduction mechanism in intrinsic semiconductors. Fabrication of high-purity semiconductors.
Electron mobility. Electrical conduction in metals
Extrinsic semiconductors. Diffusion of impurities in silicon wafers
Dielectric behavior. Dielectric strength. Dielectric materials. Mott insulators
Magnetic fields and magnitudes. Types of magnetism. Ferromagnetic domains
Magnetically soft materials and magnetically hard materials
The superconducting state. Magnetic properties of superconductors
Current flow and magnetic fields in superconductors. Applications
Optical properties and superconducting materials. Stimulated emission radiation and lasers. Optical fibers
General introduction to these types of materials
Structural unit. Degree of polymerization. Molecular weight and polydispersity
Classification of polymers. Chemical and physical structure. Technological properties and applications
Behavior of thermoplastic polymers, elastomers, and thermosets
Fiber-reinforced composites. Fillers and additives. Matrices and fiber types. Manufacturing and characteristics
Definition and objectives of the test
Condition of specimens after the test
Other information provided by the test: Elastic modulus, True stress, Strain energy.
Methods for determining hardness: Mohs, Brinell, Vickers, Rockwell, Leeb, Shore, Knoop.
Fields of application for each test
Relationship between hardness and mechanical resistance
Equipment for plastic product manufacturing processes
Glass transition temperature: concept and relationship with mechanical properties
Differences between thermoplastics and thermosets (thermosetting plastics)
Tensile test, influence of applied speed

assessment_methods.method: Global exam: Metals 1 (Themes I, II, III)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 10% progressive evaluation (laboratory assignments) and 90% from a global exam. For the global exam, it is divided into four parts: Metals 1 (33.75%), Metals 2 (33.75%), Polymeric Materials (16.875%), and Ceramic Materials (5.625%). To pass, students must achieve a minimum of 4/10 in each of these four global exam parts and a weighted average of at least 5/10 for these parts, considering their individual weights. Grades of 5/10 or higher in individual global exam parts are retained for the entire academic year, including the extraordinary (resit) exam, and laboratory grades are retained indefinitely.
